description: Rhizopus soft rot is a fungal disease that mainly affects fruits, vegetables, and stored crops. The fungus infects wounded plant tissues and causes a rapid soft, watery decay. It is common during storage, transport, and in warm and humid conditions.
symptoms: Soft watery rot on infected tissues
Rapid breakdown of fruit or vegetable tissue
White cotton-like fungal growth on the surface
Black pin-like spore structures on infected areas
Infected tissues become mushy and collapse
spread: Contact between infected and healthy produce
Insects or mechanical damage that create wounds
impact: Fruit and vegetable decay during storage or transport
cultural_control: Handle fruits and vegetables carefully to avoid wounds
Remove damaged or infected produce quickly
Maintain good hygiene in storage areas
Ensure proper ventilation in storage facilities
biological_control: Use beneficial microbes such as Bacillus species
Use biocontrol yeasts that inhibit fungal growth
chemical_control: Use of disinfectants for storage containers and equipment
prevention: Store crops at appropriate temperature and humidity
Use clean containers and storage facilities
Separate infected produce from healthy produce
source: Plant pathology references on post-harvest diseases
